gadgets.versions: 10.x with QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis (measured live on Laravel 10 + predis 2.1 + redis 7.0.15)
gadgets.sink: queue payloads are neither signed nor encrypted: data.command is a plain PHP-serialized object that the worker unserializes
gadgets.effect: arbitrary object injection in the worker process. CallQueuedHandler::getCommand unserializes anything whose command string starts with 'O:' and only falls back to the Encrypter otherwise, so no key is needed. Any job property that reaches a dangerous call (a shell command, a path, a model id) is then attacker-controlled.
gadgets.precondition: a write primitive against the queue store -- an SSRF that can speak the store's protocol is enough; redis needs no auth in most challenge images
gadgets.trap: the queue key carries the redis prefix: with no APP_NAME the default is Str::slug('Laravel','_').'_database_', so the list is laravel_database_queues:default. Confirm with KEYS * rather than assuming. A job that uses SerializesModels is still fine to forge by hand -- __unserialize skips properties missing from your array. Read a genuine payload out of the list with LRANGE and diff against it before trusting your own serialization; a wrong class-name byte length is silently rejected. Finally, check the worker's --sleep value: at --sleep=600 a pushed job can sit for ten minutes, and a quiet queue is not evidence of a bad payload.
